summary: The latest completion-admission fence prevents an invalid outer completion from reentering through nested completion, dispatch, stale-action, or unmount calls. Error descriptor observation stays fenced; valid synchronous host replies see the committed pending view, queue, drain once, and reject duplicates.

preserved_n5_finding.observed_before_fix: Outer invalid Proxy was rejected after nested valid completion was accepted; Update ran twice, Count became 1, Reply was reply-from-reentrant-trap. Original source/raw were preserved unchanged.

n4_adjusted_probe.result: Nested valid reply rejected; outer invalid reply rejected; Count 0 and Reply empty; Update remains at one call for the pending request.

checked.invalid_outer_completion: one ownKeys trap; nested complete/dispatch/stale/unmount rejected; no extra host requests or updates; trace unchanged; Count 0; Reply empty; pending effect remains; runtime is mounted and not failed
checked.error_message_descriptor: getOwnPropertyDescriptor(message) trap attempted the same nested entrypoints while completion validation threw; all were rejected under the fence and state/trace/lifecycle remained unchanged
checked.synchronous_host_reply: host observed committed pending view and HTML plus two ticks; reply returned queued, then drained to one completion tick; duplicate rejected without another Update

limits: This review covers the JavaScript runtime contract and reproduced completion-admission behavior; it is not a general Go or JavaScript security audit.
Focused suite and independent probe use compiled-symbol, renderer, and effect-host stubs.
Root/N6 reports counter browser evidence as passing; form, list, and effect browser failures remain attributable to the separate React spareZero ABI-admission issue. No four-app pass is claimed here.
